newsitem.title: UK: UK charters Conakry flight for S.Leone refugees.
newsitem.headline: UK charters Conakry flight for S.Leone refugees.

text.p: Britain chartered a Boeing 747 on Wednesday to bring refugees from the conflict in Sierra Leone home, the Foreign Office said.
A spokesman said the flight, from Conakry in Guinea, would carry about 200 British people, their dependants, 75 U.S. nationals and 80 other nationals, mostly from European Union countries.

The flight, the third chartered by Britain, is likely to leave Paris around 1800 GMT, reaching Conakry at 2400 GMT. The estimated departure time from Conakry is 0400 GMT, arriving at London's Stansted airport at about 1000 GMT on Thursday.
The spokesman said the Foreign Office believed there were only six Britons left in Sierra Leone, and all those who wanted to leave had now had the opportunity to go.
At present, it was unclear which EU and British Commonwealth countries still had diplomatic representation in Sierra Leone and could therefore be asked to represent British interests there.
"We understand the French are today mounting a further evacuation from Freetown for their own and other nationals who want to leave," the spokesman said.
Earlier, U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan and British Foreign Secretary Robin Cook said a military solution might have to be considered as a last resort to reinstate civilian rule in Sierra Leone.

Annan and Cook told reporters after an hour-long meeting they both preferred a peaceful end to the stand-off between junior officers who led a coup on May 25 and Nigerian forces trying to restore democracy in the west African country.
